messages:
support_jamie: Hey team — customer reports repeated SSE disconnects and lots of partial outputs. They say client reconnects but sees missing tokens and duplicate billing events. Started ~12:05 UTC.

sre_miguel: Got it. Do we have a request_id or example stream token from the user?

support_jamie: They sent a request_id: req_01GZ9X2R5 and a minimal repro: curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/resp?model=gpt-open-1

support_jamie: Their client is a web app behind Cloudflare + our ALB. They see disconnects every ~65s.

eng_runtime_leah: 65s = suspiciously close to common LB idle timeouts (60s) + jitter. Could be ALB or Cloudflare closing idle TCP. Do we send any SSE comment pings?

support_jamie: They said server pings are set to 30s but might be comment lines (":\n"). Not sure if those are actually hitting the wire — their frontend logs show no incoming bytes between events.

devon_oncall: Repro steps I'd run: 1) curl -v -N to see raw bytes; 2) tcpdump on a host servicing that request to see if pings leave server and if FIN/RST from LB; 3) check ALB idle timeout and Cloudflare keep-alive settings.

eng_runtime_leah: Agreed. Also check TCP keepalive on the socket (SO_KEEPALIVE). Many proxies ignore TCP keepalive if they act at L7 and use their own timeouts. Best practice is to send application-level SSE comments every 15-25s. SSE comment format: a line starting with colon. Example ping: \n\n```\n: ping\n\n\n\n```\n
eng_runtime_leah: That is important — "comment pings" are valid SSE and most clients (EventSource) keep the connection open. Some proxies don't treat empty newlines as activity, so include a small payload comment.

sre_miguel: Also check ALB settings: default idle timeout is 60s for Classic/ALB. If the LB doesn't see data, it will send TCP RST/FIN. Cloudflare has a 100s idle time for websockets but may close earlier.

support_jamie: The customer's ALB idle timeout was 60s. They thought our server pinged every 30s, but looking at logs we only emitted internal pings in our app layer and they were filtered by a middleware for empty events. Looks like the middleware removed comment lines unless flagged.

eng_runtime_leah: Oof. Two issues: middleware removed comment pings (so no keepalive bytes), and ALB closed at 60s. Fix paths: 1) re-enable SSE comment pings so bytes are emitted; 2) add Last-Event-ID handling with event `id:` on streaming tokens to allow resume; 3) recommend ALB idle timeout >= 120s for long sessions, or configure proxy to allow 1-minute pings.

devon_oncall: For partial output/dedup & billing: if client reconnects and we re-run tokens, customer could be billed twice. We should issue a session_id on stream start and accept a `Last-Event-ID` header or `last_event_id` param to dedupe. Also have server-side idempotency keys per-session so resumed sessions continue from the last acknowledged token.

support_jamie: Customer asked for concrete repro instructions. I drafted this and want review before sending: \n1) Run: `curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-open-1"` and watch for `: ping` lines every 30s. If you don't see them, connection is idle and LB might drop it.\n2) If using EventSource in browser, open devtools & look at Network tab. Check for `Last-Event-ID` header on reconnects.\n3) Capture TCP trace: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 port 443 -w sse.pcap` and inspect with Wireshark for RST/FIN from client or LB.

eng_runtime_leah: Looks good. Add a minimal Node fetch example that sets `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect and exponential backoff. Example: \n\n```js\nconst es = new EventSource(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}` } });\n// on reconnect, set ?last_event_id=... or set header 'Last-Event-ID'\n```\n
sre_miguel: Operational checklist: \n- Metric: sse.pings_sent (per-host)\n- Metric: sse.disconnects (reason tags: client, proxy, server)\n- Trace: correlate request_id to ALB request ids (X-Amzn-Trace-Id / X-Request-Id).

support_jamie: Customer also reported partial outputs — some tokens are missing after reconnect. Root cause likely resume not aligned (server emitted token N but client only acked N-3). Need a clear ACK protocol: client should send last-accepted-token-offset on reconnect, or at minimum use event ids at sentence or chunk boundaries.

eng_runtime_leah: We can implement sequence numbers in SSE `id:` field per chunk. On reconnect, the client sends `Last-Event-ID` and server skips tokens < last_id. Also consider emitting `event: flushed` after durable commit so clients know what was persisted for billing.

support_jamie: Billing implications: billing_bot suggested tying billing to `session_id` + sequence number, not raw connection duration. billing_bot: recommended approach: bill on finalized chunks (flushed events) and avoid double-charge by merging resumed session sequences; provide easy refund path if duplicates occur.

billing_bot: If duplicates are charged, support should: 1) fetch session events, 2) detect overlap, 3) credit later duplicates. We'll need logs to correlate.

devon_oncall: Quick mitigation for customer: push a patch to ensure SSE comment pings are not stripped and set pings every 20s. Recommend ALB idle timeout -> 120s for now. Add a short-term server toggle so we can enable portable pings per-customer.

eng_runtime_leah: I'll open a canary rollout for the ping re-enable in runtime. Patch will add config `sse.ping_interval_ms` default 20000 and ensure middleware doesn't strip comments. Also add `sse.emit_chunk_id = true`.

deploy_bot: deploy queued for canary pool: canary-3 hosts. ETA ~15m.

sre_miguel: After deploy, we'll monitor sse.disconnects and ALB connection resets. Devon, can you coordinate with customer to flip the switch and test while we watch?

devon_oncall: Yep, I'm on the call with them at 13:20 UTC. Will also collect tcpdump and EventSource logs.

support_jamie: Thanks all. I'll send the repro + short explanation to customer and attach these steps. Will update thread after test. :thumbsup:

support_jamie: UPDATE 13:45 UTC — canary patch deployed, customer reports stable connection for 40 minutes with pings every 20s, no billing duplicates observed so far. They will run longer tests tonight.

sre_miguel: Great. Action items: \n- eng_runtime_leah: roll the ping and chunk id flag to 100% after validation.\n- eng_runtime_leah: implement server-side session_id + `event:id` sequencing for resume semantics (spec and timeline).\n- support_jamie: follow up if any duplicate charges and collect traces for billing_bot.

eng_runtime_leah: Will file a PR/Ticket and link here. Also add docs on recommended ALB/CF timeout settings and client reconnect patterns.

support_jamie: Closing for now, will reopen if customer sees further issues. :white_check_mark:
